lesson.title: Ask, count, tally
lesson.subtitle: Data answers a question, and tally marks count it fast

video.title: Ask, count, tally
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — the class teacher (main character)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Everyone shouts; Which snack?; What do most want?. Amina beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our class is choosing a snack for Sports Day. Everyone shouted at once! How can we find out what most of you want?

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: ask a question, collect the answers, and count them.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: A question; Everyone answers; Data: the answers.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Data is facts we collect to answer a question. Our question: which snack do you like best? Each answer is one piece of data.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: One line for each answer; Four lines, then one across; Count in fives: 5, 10, 15.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: To count fast, use tally marks. Draw one line for each answer. Four lines, then the fifth goes across them. Then count in fives: five, ten, fifteen!

scenes.visual: A bar chart that draws itself: 12, 7, 9 (Votes for each snack).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here are our answers. Oranges: twelve. Bananas: seven. Mangoes: nine. Oranges win!

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! How do you write seven with tally marks?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: A group of five; Two more lines; Seven!.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: One group of five, with the fifth line across, and two more lines. Groups of five make counting quick, and hard to get wrong.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Computers count exactly what is written. If one list says Musa and another says Moussa, the computer thinks there are two pupils!

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: 20 names; Match the list; 8 pupils.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, two teachers wrote the same class list in different ways. Tap “Match the class list”. Watch the computer's count go from twenty names to eight pupils!

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A list says Musa, Moussa and Musah. How many pupils can a computer see?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Data answers a question; Tally in fives; Write names one way; Count carefully. Takeaway bar: A good question, then careful counting.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Three: to a computer, every way of writing is a different name. Remember: data is facts we collect to answer a question. Tally marks count fast, in fives. And always count carefully.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Ask ten people; One question; Tally, then count; Which answer won?. Amina beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: ask ten people at home or at school one question. What's your favourite fruit, maybe? Keep a tally, then count. Which answer won?

checkpoints.prompt: How do you write seven with tally marks?

options.text: One group of five, and two more lines
A 7 with a line across it

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — four lines, a fifth across them, then two more: seven.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — tally marks go in groups of five: four lines and one across. Then two more lines make seven.

checkpoints.prompt: A list says “Musa”, “Moussa” and “Musah”. How many pupils can a computer see?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the computer counts exactly what is written, so three spellings are three names.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — we know it's one pupil, but the computer counts each spelling as a different name: three.
